lessons.title: Cleaning Groundnuts: Removing Stones, Dirt, and Bad Nuts
lessons.body: Cleaning groundnuts is the first and most important step in making good peanut butter. Dirty nuts can spoil the taste and even make people sick. Start by spreading your raw groundnuts on a clean tarpaulin or a large wooden tray in a thin layer. Pick out stones, sticks, and any foreign matter by hand. This is best done in small batches so you don't miss anything. A simple trick is to run your fingers through the nuts and feel for hard objects. For larger amounts, use a sieve or a locally made wire mesh to shake out dirt and small stones. You can also use a fan or the wind to blow away light chaff and dust. After dry cleaning, wash the nuts in clean water if they are very dirty. Soak them for 5-10 minutes, rub them between your hands, then rinse until the water runs clear. Spread them out to dry in the sun for 1-2 days, or use a solar dryer. Never roast wet nuts; they must be completely dry. Next, remove bad nuts: discolor, shriveled, mouldy, or insect-damaged nuts. Mouldy nuts can contain aflatoxins, which are dangerous. Discard them immediately. A good rule: if in doubt, throw it out. For consistent quality, do this cleaning step every time, even if the nuts look clean. Aim to remove at least 99% of foreign matter. A 50 kg bag of raw groundnuts typically yields about 45 kg of clean nuts after removing stones, dirt, and bad nuts. This step takes time but ensures a safe and tasty final product. Remember, clean nuts make clean peanut butter.

lessons.title: Roasting Methods: Pan Roasting, Sand Roasting, and Oven Roasting
lessons.body: Roasting brings out the flavour and makes peeling easier. There are three common methods: pan roasting, sand roasting, and oven roasting. Pan roasting: Use a heavy-bottomed pan, like a cast iron or thick aluminium pot. Heat it over medium fire. Add a single layer of clean, dry groundnuts. Stir constantly with a wooden spoon to avoid burning. Roast for 10-15 minutes until they are golden brown and smell nutty. This method is good for small batches (1-2 kg). Sand roasting: Heat clean, dry sand in a large pot or pan. The sand should be hot but not smoking. Add groundnuts and stir continuously. The sand helps distribute heat evenly and prevents burning. Roast for 8-12 minutes. Then separate the nuts from the sand using a sieve. This method is faster and works well for larger batches (5-10 kg). Oven roasting: Preheat an oven to 160-180Â°C. Spread groundnuts in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. This method is less labour-intensive but requires an oven. For all methods, the key is constant stirring and watching closely. The nuts will darken and release oil. Test by taking a few out, cooling, and tasting. They should be crunchy, not soft. Over-roasting makes them bitter and oily; under-roasting makes peeling hard and flavour weak. After roasting, cool the nuts completely before peeling. Roasting also kills bacteria and reduces moisture, which helps the peanut butter last longer. For a 10 kg batch, pan roasting takes about 45 minutes, sand roasting 30 minutes, and oven roasting 25 minutes. Always roast in a well-ventilated area.

lessons.title: Determining Perfect Roast: Color, Aroma, and Taste Tests
lessons.body: Knowing when groundnuts are perfectly roasted is a skill you can learn with practice. You need to check three things: colour, aroma, and taste. Colour: Raw groundnuts are pale, whitish-yellow. As they roast, they turn light brown, then golden brown, and finally dark brown. The perfect roast is a uniform golden brown. If they are still pale, they need more time. If they are dark brown or black, they are over-roasted and will taste bitter. Aroma: Raw nuts smell earthy. As they roast, they release a rich, nutty aroma. When you can smell that strong, pleasant nutty smell, they are close to done. If you smell a burnt or acrid smell, they are over-roasting. Taste: The most reliable test. Take a few nuts out, let them cool for a minute (they are hot!), and taste. Perfectly roasted nuts are crunchy, slightly sweet, and have a deep nutty flavour. If they taste raw or bland, roast longer. If they taste bitter or burnt, you've gone too far. Another test: rub a nut between your fingers. The skin should come off easily. If the skin sticks, they need more roasting. Also, listen for a crackling sound as they roast; when the crackling slows down, they are nearly done. For consistent results, roast in small batches and check every 2 minutes after the first 10 minutes. Record the time and temperature that works for your setup. Different groundnut varieties and sizes roast at different rates. For example, small nuts roast faster than large ones. Always preheat your pan or oven. After roasting, spread the nuts on a cool tray to stop the cooking process. Do not pile them up, as they will continue to cook from residual heat. Perfect roast is key to great peanut butter.

lessons.title: Peeling Groundnuts: Manual and Mechanical Methods
lessons.body: After roasting and cooling, the next step is peeling off the skins. Peeling is important because skins can make peanut butter bitter and gritty. There are manual and mechanical methods. Manual peeling: This is the most common for small-scale producers. Rub the cooled nuts between your hands or on a rough surface like a woven basket or a clean piece of burlap. The skins will flake off. For larger quantities, put nuts in a sack and beat them gently with a wooden stick, then winnow. Another manual method is to rub them on a wire mesh. This takes time: one person can peel about 2-3 kg per hour. It's labour-intensive but requires no special equipment. Mechanical peeling: If you produce larger volumes, consider a groundnut peeler. These machines range from simple hand-cranked models to motorised ones. A small motorised peeler can process 50-100 kg per hour. They work by rubbing the nuts against a rotating drum or abrasive surface. You can find these machines from agricultural suppliers or fabricators. They cost between $200 and $1000, depending on capacity. When using a mechanical peeler, adjust the spacing so it doesn't break the nuts. Broken nuts are fine for peanut butter, but whole nuts look better if you sell them. After peeling, you must separate the skins from the nuts. This is done by winnowing (see next lesson). Peeling efficiency: manual methods remove about 80-90% of skins; mechanical methods can remove 95% or more. Some skins may remain, especially in the crevices. You can rub the nuts again or use a fan to blow away loose skins. Don't worry if a few skins remain; they won't ruin the peanut butter. But too many skins make it bitter. After peeling, use the nuts immediately or store them in an airtight container to prevent them from absorbing moisture. Peeling is easier when nuts are roasted and cooled completely. If nuts are still warm, skins stick.

lessons.title: Cooling and Winnowing to Remove Skins
lessons.body: After roasting, groundnuts must be cooled completely before peeling. Cooling stops the cooking process and makes skins brittle and easy to remove. Spread the hot nuts in a single layer on a clean, dry tray or mat. Do not pile them up, as trapped heat will cause them to steam and become soft. Let them cool for 20-30 minutes at room temperature. You can speed cooling by using a fan, but avoid blowing dust onto the nuts. Once cooled, the skins will be loose and flaky. Now, winnowing: This is the process of separating the skins from the nuts. The traditional method is to toss the nuts in the air using a winnowing basket or a flat tray. The wind blows away the lighter skins while the heavier nuts fall back. Do this on a windy day or use a fan. Stand with your back to the wind, hold the basket, and toss the nuts gently. The skins fly away, and the nuts land back in the basket. Repeat until most skins are removed. For small quantities, you can also use a hair dryer on cool setting or an electric fan. Another method is to pour the nuts from one container to another in front of a fan. The skins blow away. For larger scale, use a mechanical winnower, which is a machine that uses air to separate skins. These are available from agricultural equipment suppliers. After winnowing, check for any remaining skins. You can rub the nuts again and winnow once more. Aim to remove at least 95% of skins. Remaining skins are okay but can add bitterness. Winnowing also removes any small stones or debris that were missed. Do this in a well-ventilated area, as the dust can be irritating. Wear a mask if you are sensitive. After winnowing, your nuts are ready for grinding into peanut butter. Store them in a clean, dry container. If you are not grinding immediately, keep them in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. They will stay fresh for up to 2 weeks. Proper cooling and winnowing ensure a smooth, tasty peanut butter.

lessons.title: Quality Control: Ensuring Consistent Roast and Cleanliness
lessons.body: Quality control is what separates a good peanut butter from a great one. You need to ensure every batch is consistent in roast and cleanliness. Start by setting standards. For roast, decide on a target colour (e.g., golden brown) and aroma. Use a colour chart or sample photos. Train yourself to recognise the perfect roast by sight, smell, and taste. For cleanliness, aim for zero foreign matter, stones, or bad nuts. Implement checks at each step. After cleaning, inspect a handful of nuts for stones or dirt. After roasting, check colour and taste. After peeling and winnowing, check for remaining skins. Keep a record of times, temperatures, and batch sizes. This helps you repeat success. Use simple tools: a thermometer for oven roasting, a timer, and a scale. For pan roasting, use a timer and your senses. Consistency also means uniform roasting. If you roast unevenly, some nuts will be burnt and others raw. To avoid this, roast in small batches, stir constantly, and use a single layer. For large batches, use a mechanical roaster, like a drum roaster, which rotates for even roasting. Cleanliness also means hygiene. Wash your hands, wear clean clothes, and keep your work area clean. Use clean water for washing. Store nuts in clean, covered containers. Avoid contamination from pests. If you find mouldy nuts, discard them and clean the area. Aflatoxins are a serious health risk. Test for moisture: good roasted nuts should have less than 6% moisture. You can use a moisture meter or the salt test: put a nut in a saturated salt solution; if it floats, moisture is too high. For small producers, simply ensure nuts are dry and crunchy. Finally, do a final quality check before grinding. Taste a few nuts. They should be crunchy, nutty, and free of off-flavours. If they are not perfect, adjust your process. Consistent quality builds customer trust and allows you to charge a better price. Keep a notebook and review your notes regularly.

quiz.q: Why is it important to remove mouldy groundnuts?
options: C) They are hard to peel
D) They make the oil dark
quiz.explanation: Mouldy groundnuts can contain aflatoxins, which are dangerous to health.

quiz.q: What is the first step in cleaning groundnuts?
quiz.explanation: Hand-picking removes large foreign matter before further cleaning.

quiz.q: How long should you sun-dry washed groundnuts?
quiz.explanation: Sun-drying for 1-2 days ensures nuts are completely dry before roasting.

quiz.q: Which roasting method uses hot sand?
quiz.explanation: Sand roasting involves heating groundnuts with hot sand for even heat distribution.

quiz.q: What is a sign that groundnuts are perfectly roasted?
options: C) They are golden brown and smell nutty
quiz.explanation: Golden brown colour and nutty aroma indicate perfect roast.

quiz.q: Why should you cool groundnuts before peeling?
options: B) To make skins brittle and easy to remove
D) To prevent burning your hands only
quiz.explanation: Cooling makes skins brittle, so they flake off easily during peeling.

quiz.q: What is winnowing?
options: B) Separating skins from nuts using air
quiz.explanation: Winnowing uses air to blow away lighter skins from heavier nuts.

quiz.q: How can you test if roasted groundnuts are over-roasted?
options: B) They taste bitter and burnt
quiz.explanation: Over-roasted nuts taste bitter and burnt due to excessive heat.

quiz.q: What is a manual method for peeling groundnuts?
options: B) Rubbing between hands or on a rough surface
quiz.explanation: Rubbing cooled nuts between hands or on a rough surface removes skins manually.

quiz.q: What percentage of skins should be removed for good quality?
quiz.explanation: Removing at least 95% of skins prevents bitterness and grit in peanut butter.

quiz.q: Why is quality control important in peanut butter production?
options: B) To ensure consistent taste and safety
quiz.explanation: Quality control ensures every batch is safe, tasty, and consistent for customers.

quiz.q: What should you do if groundnuts smell burnt during roasting?
quiz.explanation: Burnt smell means over-roasting; remove immediately to prevent bitterness.

quiz.q: Which tool can help you achieve even roasting in large batches?
quiz.explanation: A drum roaster rotates for even heat distribution in large batches.

quiz.q: What is the ideal moisture content for roasted groundnuts?
quiz.explanation: Low moisture (less than 6%) ensures crunchiness and longer shelf life.

quiz.q: How can you remove remaining skins after winnowing?
options: B) Rub nuts again and winnow
quiz.explanation: Rubbing and winnowing again helps remove stubborn skins.

quiz.q: What is a sign that groundnuts need more roasting?
options: C) They are pale and skins stick
quiz.explanation: Pale colour and sticking skins indicate under-roasting.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid piling hot groundnuts after roasting?
options: A) They will cool too fast
B) They will continue cooking and steam
C) They will become too dry
quiz.explanation: Piling traps heat, causing nuts to steam and become soft instead of crispy.

quiz.q: What is a mechanical peeler?
options: B) A machine that rubs nuts to remove skins
quiz.explanation: Mechanical peelers use rotating drums or abrasive surfaces to remove skins efficiently.

quiz.q: How can you check for stones after cleaning?
options: B) Feel a handful of nuts
quiz.explanation: Feeling a handful helps detect hard objects like stones that may have been missed.

quiz.q: What is the benefit of sand roasting over pan roasting?
options: B) It distributes heat evenly and prevents burning
quiz.explanation: Sand distributes heat evenly, reducing the risk of burning and allowing larger batches.

quiz.q: Why is it important to record roasting times and temperatures?
options: B) To repeat success and ensure consistency
quiz.explanation: Records help you replicate the perfect roast for every batch.

quiz.q: What should you do with broken nuts after peeling?
options: B) Use them for peanut butter
C) Sell them as whole nuts
quiz.explanation: Broken nuts are fine for peanut butter, as they will be ground anyway.

quiz.q: How can you test if groundnuts are dry enough for storage?
options: B) They are crunchy and skins crack
quiz.explanation: Crunchy nuts with cracking skins indicate low moisture and readiness for storage.

quiz.q: What is aflatoxin?
options: B) A poisonous substance from mould
quiz.explanation: Aflatoxin is a dangerous toxin produced by moulds on poorly stored nuts.

quiz.q: Why should you wear a mask during winnowing?
options: B) To prevent inhaling dust from skins
quiz.explanation: Winnowing creates dust from skins that can irritate the lungs.

quiz.q: What is the target colour for perfectly roasted groundnuts?
quiz.explanation: Golden brown indicates ideal roast, balancing flavour and crunch.

quiz.q: How long can roasted, peeled groundnuts be stored in an airtight container?
quiz.explanation: In a cool, dry place, they stay fresh for up to 2 weeks.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a moisture meter?
options: B) To measure water content in nuts
quiz.explanation: A moisture meter checks if nuts are dry enough for storage and grinding.

quiz.q: Why is constant stirring important during pan roasting?
options: B) To prevent burning and ensure even roasting
quiz.explanation: Stirring prevents nuts from sticking and burning, ensuring uniform colour and flavour.

quiz.q: What should you do if you find stones in cleaned groundnuts?
quiz.explanation: Stones can damage equipment and teeth, so they must be removed before further processing.
